meta.title: Fosta Studio: a small, fast, open-source database client
meta.description: Free, open-source database client built in Rust: an AI agent that understands your database, MCP, multiple workspaces and tunnels that start on their own.
meta.socialDescription: Built in Rust: an AI agent that understands your database structure, MCP support, multiple workspaces and tunnels that start on their own. Free and open source.
meta.ogImageAlt: Fosta Studio logo, an F made of data rows, with the text: free, open-source database client for 11 engines, built in Rust
nav.label: Primary
hero.lede: A database client built in Rust, with an AI agent that understands your database structure, MCP support, multiple workspaces and tunnels that start on their own. Free and open source. Supports 11 databases, from MariaDB and PostgreSQL to MongoDB, Redis and Oracle.
hero.macNote: On a Mac? There is no native macOS app yet, but the web edition runs on your Mac: install Docker Desktop, run these commands, then use Fosta Studio in your browser.
hero.note: Version {version} · Windows installer or portable .exe · macOS and Linux through the Docker web edition
hero.smartscreen: Windows may show a SmartScreen warning because the app is not code-signed yet: choose More info → Run anyway.
hero.dockerNote: Then open the sign-in address printed in the log. Web edition guide

why.title: Fast where it counts, careful where it matters
why.intro: A native client for developers who move between projects, engines and environments all day, and would rather not break production on the way.
stats.label: Fosta Studio in numbers
stats.size: installer download; a portable .exe needs no install
stats.ai: AI providers, from Claude and GPT to local models
why.native.title: Native, small and quick
why.native.text: A Rust core in a Tauri 2 shell with a plain TypeScript UI and a virtualised grid. The installer is about 9 MB, and the app leaves your memory to the databases.
why.engines.title: A view that fits each engine
why.engines.text: SQL tables open in an editable grid. Redis keys, Elasticsearch search, ClickHouse parts and Oracle PL/SQL each get a view of their own instead of being squeezed into rows.
why.workspaces.title: Workspaces that open their own tunnels
why.workspaces.text: Each project or environment keeps its connections, tabs and startup tasks. Open it and kubectl port-forward starts, restarts when it drops, and stops when you quit.
why.gateway.title: Production stays read-only
why.gateway.text: Every statement, on every engine, passes one gateway with rules per workspace. A Production workspace defaults to read-only, and risky statements ask for confirmation first.
why.open.title: Open source, desktop or Docker
why.open.text: GPL-3.0, no account, no telemetry. A Windows desktop app, or a web edition that starts with one docker run.
why.ai.title: An AI agent that knows your schema
why.ai.text: Ask in plain words. The agent explores tables and relations, writes and explains queries, opens the right view and reads task logs to help you debug. Use Claude, GPT, Gemini, Fosta or a local Ollama model.
features.title: Built for the way you work with data
features.intro: From the first query of the day to the last migration check, the everyday work stays quick, visible and under your control.
query.title: A query editor that keeps up
query.text: Syntax highlighting, a formatter and completion that knows your tables and columns, for SQL, MongoDB commands and Redis. Several statements per run; each tab keeps its own session, so BEGIN…COMMIT can span runs.
query.item1: Every run lands in a searchable history that stays on your machine
query.item2: Results open in the same grid as tables, ready to filter and export
query.item3: Streaming results that show the first rows at once, and a Stop that really cancels on the server
query.caption: A query typed, run and answered in the grid (illustration).
ws.title: Workspaces and startup tasks
ws.text: Group connections, startup tasks and open tabs per project, customer or environment, then switch from the rail on the left or with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>1…9</kbd>. Tabs of other workspaces stay open.
ws.item1: Bind kubectl port-forward to a connection: it starts when you connect and stops when you disconnect
ws.item2: Automatic restart with backoff when a tunnel drops, and live logs
ws.item3: Child processes are cleaned up when the app exits
ws.shotAlt: Fosta Studio with several workspaces in the rail and the startup task log of a kubectl port-forward.
ws.caption: Each workspace brings its own connections, tasks and tabs.
grid.title: A data grid made for editing
grid.text: A virtualised grid that pages through large tables, with type badges under each column name so you always know what you are looking at.
grid.item1: Inline editing, inserts and deletes collected in a pending-changes bar
grid.item2: Apply the changes together, or discard them; a row someone else changed is a conflict, not an overwrite
grid.item4: A record panel that follows foreign keys to related rows
grid.shotAlt: The Fosta Studio data grid with column filters, type badges, an edited cell and the pending changes bar.
grid.caption: Edits wait in the pending bar until you apply them.
diagram.title: Interactive ER diagrams
diagram.text: See how a database fits together. The diagram lays itself out automatically; drag tables around, zoom in, and export the result.
diagram.shotAlt: An ER diagram of a shop database in Fosta Studio, with tables connected by foreign keys.
diagram.caption: Tables and their foreign keys, laid out for you.
ai.title: A built-in AI agent for your databases
ai.text: Ask in plain words. The agent looks up tables, columns and relations, writes and explains queries, fixes errors, and opens a table, a diagram or a new query tab for you. Every code block has Run, Insert and New tab buttons.
ai.callout: You stay in control. Run on a code block follows your workspace's safety rules, like any run of your own. The agent's own queries are read-only, and you can turn them off.
ai.item1: Bring your own model: Fosta, OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as a local Ollama
ai.item2: Your key is stored in Windows Credential Manager and requests go straight from your machine to the provider
ai.item3: It sees metadata and what you share; the optional read-only query tool can read up to 50 rows, which go to your provider
ai.disclosure: Disclosure: Fosta, the default provider, is a separate AI API service run by the author of Fosta Studio. It is listed first for convenience only; nothing in Fosta Studio requires a Fosta account, and requests only go to the provider you configure.
ai.shotAlt: The Fosta Studio assistant panel with a question, a suggested SQL query and the Insert and New tab buttons.
ai.caption: From question to a ready-to-run query in seconds.
mini.io.title: Import & export
mini.io.text: Import CSV, TSV or JSON with column mapping. Export to CSV, CSV for Excel, JSON, SQL INSERT statements or Markdown.
mini.vector.title: Vector tools
mini.vector.text: Embedding search, column and index health checks, and index recall against exact search on MariaDB 11.7+, PostgreSQL (pgvector), Oracle 23ai, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Redis 8 and ClickHouse.
mini.conn.title: Connections, SSH and TLS
mini.conn.text: Paste a connection string for any engine. Add an SSH tunnel with a jump host or agent, and TLS with your CA, a client certificate or a pinned fingerprint. Passwords stay in Credential Manager.
mini.cell.title: Cell editor
mini.cell.text: Press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> on a long value for a large editor with NULL, word wrap, and Format / Minify with validation for JSON.
engines.title: One client for the databases you actually run
engines.intro: Each engine is a native Rust driver behind one shared interface, so workspaces, safety rules and the assistant work the same everywhere, while each engine gets a view that fits its data.
engines.mysql: Stop a running query from the editor
engines.mongodb: JSON filters, Atlas URIs, inferred diagram links, commands in the query tab
engines.redis: Key browser with an editor for each data type, console with completion, vector tools on Redis 8; also Valkey
engines.elastic: Mapping-typed grid, Dev Tools console, ES|QL and SQL, vector tools
privacy.title: Your data stays yours
privacy.intro: Fosta Studio talks to your databases and to the AI provider you configure. Nothing else.
privacy.config.title: Local, portable config
privacy.config.text: Workspaces, connections and tasks live in fosta-studio.json next to the executable. No secrets are written to it.
privacy.creds.title: Windows Credential Manager
privacy.creds.text: Database passwords and AI keys are stored in the operating system's credential store, never in the config file.
privacy.telemetry.title: No telemetry, no account
privacy.telemetry.text: No telemetry and no sign-up. The only call home is a daily check on GitHub for a new version, which you can turn off in Settings. It is fully usable offline with local databases.
privacy.ai.title: What the agent sees
privacy.ai.text: The model sees table and column metadata plus the editor text, errors and logs you choose to share. Statements run only when you run them. The optional read-only query tool reads up to 50 rows per query, which go to your provider; turn it off in Settings or per workspace.
privacy.gateway.title: Statement gateway
privacy.gateway.text: Every statement, on every engine, passes through one gateway with rules per workspace: Open, Guarded, Read-only or Custom. A workspace marked Production defaults to Read-only, and relaxing a rule always comes with a loud warning.
privacy.link: Security details: what is stored where, and what is sent
roadmap.title: Where it is heading
roadmap.intro: Planned work, roughly in order. Plans change; open an issue to discuss any of it.
roadmap.gateway.title: Engine depth
roadmap.gateway.text: Oracle without Instant Client, Redis Cluster and Sentinel, and more tools per engine.
roadmap.profiling.title: Data profiling & generation
roadmap.profiling.text: Column statistics and histograms; rule-based test data with preview before insert.
roadmap.backup.title: Backup & restore
roadmap.backup.text: Logical dumps built by the app, no external tools required.
roadmap.mongo.title: MongoDB beyond Compass
roadmap.mongo.text: A query bar with autocomplete, document views and an aggregation builder.
roadmap.servers.title: Local database servers
roadmap.servers.text: Create and run development servers without Docker or admin rights.
roadmap.web.title: Signed builds & sync
roadmap.web.text: Code-signed installers, winget and Scoop packages, and end-to-end encrypted sync between machines.
oss.title: Free software, built in the open
oss.license: Fosta Studio is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0. Use it, study it, change it and share it.
oss.cla: Contributions are welcome. On your first pull request you are asked to sign the Contributor License Agreement: you keep the copyright in your work, and the maintainer may also offer commercial licenses while the project itself stays GPL.
build.title: Build from source
build.text: Prefer to build it yourself? You need Node 20+, Rust 1.88+ and the MSVC or GNU toolchain (toolchain details).
build.result: The result is src-tauri\target\release\fosta-studio.exe. Want to try the UI first? npm run dev previews it in a browser with sample data.
footer.tagline: Free and open-source database client. GPL-3.0.
footer.trademarks: MariaDB, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, ClickHouse and Oracle are trademarks of their respective owners. Fosta Studio is an independent project and is not affiliated with them.
lang.label: Language
engines.postgres: Schemas, jsonb and arrays, Stop on the server, EXPLAIN, vector tools with pgvector
engines.sqlite: Open a file, attach databases, edit by primary key or rowid
engines.clickhouse: Streaming queries, edits as mutations, parts and query log, vector search on Array columns
engines.oracle: PL/SQL and packages, vector tools on 23ai; Instant Client is downloaded for you
engines.opensearch: The same grid and console, SQL plugin, point-in-time paging, vector tools
dbp.meta.title: Databases: what Fosta Studio supports on each engine
dbp.meta.description: The 11 engines of Fosta Studio, from MariaDB and PostgreSQL to Redis, Elasticsearch and Oracle: tested versions, what works on each, engine-specific views and vector tools.
dbp.title: Eleven engines, one client
dbp.intro: What works on each engine, the server versions the test suites run against, and the views made for each one. Every engine is a native Rust driver behind one shared interface.
dbp.matrix.title: At a glance
dbp.matrix.label: Feature matrix, scrolls sideways
dbp.matrix.legend: ✓ available, — not available. Redis is edited in its key browser, and ClickHouse edits run as mutations. Vector tools need MariaDB 11.7+, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Oracle 23ai, Elasticsearch 8.0+, OpenSearch with the k-NN plugin, Redis 8 (search module) or ClickHouse 25.8+ (Array columns with a vector_similarity index).
dbp.cards.title: Engine by engine
dbp.cards.intro: “Tested with” is the server version the CI contract suites run against. Each card links to the engine's notes in the repository.
dbp.mysql.works: Typed grid with inline edits, query tabs with Stop (KILL QUERY), transactions across runs, statement timeouts, design view and ER diagram, SSH and TLS.
dbp.mariadb.vectors: On 11.7 and newer: embedding search, column and index health checks, and index recall against exact search.
dbp.mariadb.notes: A Read-only workspace also opens read-only sessions.
dbp.mysql.notes: Same driver as MariaDB (mysql_async). The vector tools are for MariaDB 11.7+ only.
dbp.mssql.works: schema.table names (dbo is hidden), OFFSET/FETCH paging, batches that return every result set and row count, query tabs with Stop, transactions, design view and ER diagram, SSH.
dbp.mssql.notes: TLS is on by default. An untrusted certificate shows an “Accept invalid certificates” hint.
dbp.postgres.works: Schemas, materialized views, functions, sequences, types and extensions; arrays, jsonb and uuid values; a Stop that cancels on the server; EXPLAIN; transactions across runs; design view and an ER diagram over all user schemas; SSH and TLS.
dbp.postgres.vectors: With pgvector: vector and halfvec columns, HNSW and IVFFlat indexes, search by cosine, L2 or inner product, health checks and index recall.
dbp.postgres.notes: Client key files must be unencrypted. LISTEN/NOTIFY, COPY streams and logical replication are not supported.
dbp.oracle.works: Schemas with tables, views, sequences, synonyms, packages, procedures and functions; edits by key or ROWID; Stop with OCIBreak; transactions from the toolbar; an ER diagram per schema; SSH and TLS.
dbp.oracle.views: PL/SQL source with compile errors, and ORA codes with the error position.
dbp.oracle.vectors: On 23ai: VECTOR columns, IVF and HNSW indexes, VECTOR_DISTANCE search, health checks and recall.
dbp.oracle.notes: Needs Oracle Instant Client 19c or newer. On the first connection the app offers to download Instant Client Basic Light from Oracle (about 60 MB, pinned checksum) or to use a folder with an installed client. TLS is tcps with a wallet.
dbp.mongo.works: Collections as tables with BSON-typed columns and edits, JSON filters, Atlas URIs, query tabs that run database commands as JSON, an ER diagram with inferred links between collections, SSH and TLS.
dbp.mongo.notes: No transactions, and no Stop for a running command.
dbp.redis.works: Every logical database; keys listed with SCAN, with type, TTL and memory; an editor for each data type (string, hash, list, set, sorted set, stream); TTL changes; SSH and TLS (rediss://).
dbp.redis.views: Key browser, a console with completion and Stop, and a server view with INFO and the slow log.
dbp.redis.notes: Also Valkey and other RESP servers. One standalone server: Redis Cluster and Sentinel are not supported yet.
dbp.sqlite.works: Open a file (read-only, create, :memory:) with attached databases; edits by primary key or rowid; Stop by interrupt; EXPLAIN; transactions; design view and ER diagram.
dbp.sqlite.notes: SQLite is bundled with the app. A database is a local file, so there is no SSH or TLS. Encrypted databases (SQLCipher) and extensions are not supported.
dbp.clickhouse.works: Databases, tables, views, materialized views and dictionaries; keyset paging; streaming query tabs that stop with KILL QUERY; a design view with the sorting key and skipping indexes; SSH and TLS.
dbp.clickhouse.views: Edits as asynchronous mutations on MergeTree tables, a Parts and mutations view, and a Server view with running queries and the query log.
dbp.clickhouse.notes: Uses the HTTP interface. No transactions, and no ER diagram (ClickHouse has no foreign keys); mutations cannot be rolled back.
dbp.es.works: Indices, data streams and aliases; a document grid typed by the mapping, with structured and Query DSL filters; search_after paging past 10,000 documents; Mapping as the design view; SSH and TLS.
dbp.es.views: A Dev Tools console (METHOD /path with JSON or NDJSON bodies), plus ES|QL and SQL tabs.
dbp.es.vectors: On 8.0 and newer: dense_vector fields, search, health checks and index recall.
dbp.es.notes: Elasticsearch 7.10 or newer. No transactions: a save checks each document's version and stops with a conflict if it changed.
dbp.os.works: The same document grid, filters and paging as Elasticsearch; basic auth or a bearer token; SSH and TLS.
dbp.os.views: The Dev Tools console and SQL tabs through the SQL plugin (no ES|QL).
dbp.os.vectors: With the k-NN plugin: knn_vector fields, search, health checks and index recall.
dbp.os.notes: OpenSearch 1.0 or newer; point-in-time paging past 10,000 hits needs 2.4.

mini.mcp.title: MCP server for AI agents
mini.mcp.text: AI agents such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor can use your connections through MCP. It is off by default, and each workspace is set to Off, Read-only or Ask before writes. Every write needs your approval in the app, every call is audited, and Production workspaces are always read-only. MCP guide
dbp.redis.vectors: With the search module (built into Redis 8): indexes with VECTOR fields (FLAT or HNSW) open as tables, with vector search and health checks. Redis 7.4 without the module has no vector tools.
dbp.clickhouse.vectors: Array(Float32), Array(Float64) or Array(BFloat16) columns with a vector_similarity index: vector search and health checks. Generally available in 25.8; older servers need an experimental setting.

dbp.shared.mcp.text: AI agents such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor can use your connections through MCP. Off by default; every write needs approval and every call is audited. MCP guide
